task: W2-68 batch 3 of 3: run the trial (DEC-884 item 4) on a fixture programme built from scratch, write its results into section 10 of the design note, commit the note, then run the suites and report their counts.
status: DONE. The trial was measured, section 10 is committed in `7a32a421`, and every suite finished before the stop, all green. No code changed, because the trial found no defect.
work_completed: I built a fixture programme from scratch in the sandbox's temp folder and measured the five observables. (1) Time per batch: a batch of 2 took 140.0 s against 142.2 s for the queue's one-by-one closes; a batch of 3 took 149.1 s against 210.1 s, 29 % faster. (2) Reuse is correct. (3) A planted code change forces a fresh run. (4) A planted record-only commit runs the record-reading set and nothing else. (5) A red batch is attributed by bisect to PROJ-bbbb, its flaky test is a candidate and is not bisected, and nothing closes on it. A second red run also showed point F: a plain close of an unrelated ticket is refused with RED_RUN_ON_CODE. All of this, with the fixture's shape, the commands, the times table, the load during each run and the caveats, is in section 10 of `docs/research/W2-68-batched-close.md`.
files_changed: docs/research/W2-68-batched-close.md (+72 −10, commit 7a32a421; it is the only commit of this batch).
evidence: Step 0: (a) failed as required (`OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`); (b) worked (`git hash-object -w` gave 1ae28402a109…, and `git update-index --refresh` exited 0). The `gov.__file__` line was `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-68/src/gov/__init__.py`. The commit is `7a32a421` with the trailers Task: DAEO-2gc7, Role: engineer, Implements: DEC-883, DEC-889, DEC-890 and Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Before committing I checked that `.git/hooks` held only `*.sample` files. I used `gov retrieve` once, for "how to build a fixture programme for close tests": it returned FACET_UNAVAILABLE (lexical and semantic both stale) and no evidence, so I read W2-66's and W1-30's support code directly instead. I met 4 refusals, none twice for the same call: (1) the Write tool refused `.gov-runtime/scratch/W2-68-trial/trial.py` (denied by the permission settings); (2) a Bash probe write to `.gov-runtime/scratch/` was refused (permission not granted); (3) reading the launch settings file was refused (EACCES); (4) the Monitor tool was refused by the guard (DEC-685). A heredoc was also refused (DEC-409); I wrote with Edit instead. Scratch: the fixtures and the nightly's temporary worktrees were each removed when their scenario ended. At the end of the run the launch temp folder measured 172 inodes and 7.0 MB (script and logs). That folder (`/tmp/gov-launch-engineer-mxbciekk`) no longer exists in this relaunched session, so nothing of mine is left to remove.
tests: All runs used this worktree's `src/` and went to their end, after the waits (load 0.9 to 8.9 at their starts), between 03:48 and 04:27 UTC. No run was cut by the stop.
- Builder tests (test_batch_refresh, test_batch_reuse, test_fingerprint, test_fingerprint_store): 35 passed.
- tests/unit/close: 473 passed.
- tests/unit/store: 17 passed.
- tests/acceptance/W2-68: 22 passed (516.6 s). Every case passes: the 7 batch cases, 3 fingerprint cases, 5 red-batch cases and 7 reuse cases.
- tests/acceptance/W1-30: 537 passed (1403.3 s).
- tests/acceptance/W2-66: 169 passed, 1 skipped (162.6 s).
- Collection: "16747/16749 tests collected (2 deselected) in 6.37s", with no collection error.
discoveries: (a) On a small fixture, the steps a batch shares are cheap: rebuild 8 to 11 s, gov check 1 to 2 s, regression about 1 s. The close's own fixed cost of 42 to 72 s dominates; its tests take under 2 s, and its stderr shows a model's weights being loaded. So batching only pays off from about 3 tickets here. On the real programme the shared steps are about 6 min of rebuild and 7 min of check, so the saving should be far larger, but that is extrapolated, not measured. (b) In the sandbox the rebuild cannot recreate the code index (read-only `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000`), so the measured rebuilds exclude it. (c) A plain `gov close` after a red batch needs `batch refresh` first: the red record's commit moves HEAD, so without the refresh the close is refused STORE_STALE before the RED_RUN_ON_CODE hold can answer. (d) In this session the worktree's `.gov-runtime/scratch/` is refused to the engineer's Write tool, although the role file grants it (DEC-108).
risks: The fixture's times are small and load-sensitive (the batch-of-2 close of PROJ-bbbb ran while the load rose to 23), so they do not stand for the real programme. The rebuild times are a CPU Ollama's, not the shared GPU's. The untracked `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.idea` and similar files in the worktree are empty read-only placeholders the sandbox mounted at 02:28. They are not mine and I left them in place, but they make `git status` dirty.
lessons: Never heredocs; write scripts with Write and Edit into the session scratchpad. Monitor is refused; wait with a background `until` loop. Run `batch refresh` before any plain close that follows a batch's record commit. Fixture programmes need a namespace with `memory_class: governance` or the lexical index is empty. Trailers must cite decisions the fixture holds (`DEC-000`, and `DEC-883` for the batch's own commits). A decision's title must not contain ": ".
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The trial's script and logs could not be kept under the worktree's `.gov-runtime/scratch/` (the write was refused), and the launch temp folder that held them is gone after the relaunch. The figures survive only in section 10 of the note.
recommended_next_action: The lead runs its own verification of the branch at `7a32a421`, then takes W2-68 to its audit and close.
